sections.h2: Which Boyle County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Three offices touch a Boyle County tax bill, and each answers a different question. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets the assessed value and processes exemptions; the phone line is 859-238-1104. The Boyle County Sheriff's Office mails and collects the bills from its desk at 321 W. Main Street, Room 103, in Danville, and answers at 859-238-1123. The county clerk takes over any bill that goes unpaid past the spring cutoff.

The clerk's own delinquent-tax page says the sheriff never assigns a value to a property. If the number on your bill looks wrong, the PVA is the office to call, and it is best to call before you pay.

  • Value, exemptions, mailing address on the bill: PVA, 859-238-1104.
  • Paying a current bill, bill lookup: Sheriff's Office, 859-238-1123.
  • Bills from earlier years: Boyle County Clerk.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Boyle County itself?
sections.html:
Boyle County sits in central Kentucky, covers 183 square miles and has Danville as its seat. Junction City and Perryville are the other incorporated cities. The county was formed in 1842 from parts of Lincoln and Mercer counties, and the Battle of Perryville was fought here on October 8, 1862. Centre College is in Danville.

The Census Bureau counted 31,632 residents in its July 2025 estimate, up 3.3 percent from the 2020 count of 30,614. The county touches Mercer, Garrard, Lincoln, Casey, Marion and Washington counties.

Census QuickFacts figures for 2020 to 2024 give a picture of the housing stock a seller is competing in:

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $209,900, with 68.0 percent of housing units owner-occupied.
  • Median gross rent: $778, across 12,045 households.
  • Median household income: $61,159, and a mean commute of 21.3 minutes.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 94.

sections.h2: When are Boyle County tax bills due?
sections.html:
The sheriff posts a four-step schedule for each tax year, and the table below shows the one published for the 2026 bills. Payment counts as on time when it is postmarked by the date shown.

Boyle County Sheriff's Office pay schedule for 2026 bills (source: boylecountyky.gov)
Paid or postmarked byAmount owed
November 30, 2026Face amount less a 2% discount
December 31, 2026Face amount
January 31, 2027Face amount plus a 5% penalty
April 15, 2027Face amount plus a 21% penalty
After April 15, 2027Turned over to the County Clerk as delinquent

The same four-step pattern repeats every year with the dates moved forward. The sheriff's page includes a Tax Bill Web Portal that searches by bill number, map number, owner name or address. Try the name both ways, because a record filed as Doe John will not show up under John Doe.

sections.h2: Which school district bills Danville properties?
sections.html:
It depends on the street. Boyle County has two public school systems, Boyle County Schools for everything outside Danville and Danville Schools inside the city. A few parcels inside Danville city limits still belong to the Boyle County district, so the address alone does not settle it.

The city of Danville explains the consequence on its property tax page. A parcel in the Danville Independent district gets a separate school bill from the school system, reachable at 859-936-8507. A parcel in the Boyle County district has its school tax folded into the sheriff's bill. Special districts such as the library, health department or fire protection appear as extra lines on the sheriff's bill where they apply.

sections.h2: What is the Danville city tax rate per $100?
sections.html:
For 2025 the city's real property rate was 11.9 cents per $100 of assessed value, down from 14.4 cents in 2017. The state rate that year was 10.6 cents per $100. The city says it has adopted the compensating rate every year back to 2017, which means the rate fell as assessments rose.

  • Real property: 0.1190 in 2025, against 0.1440 in 2017 and 0.1220 in 2024.
  • Tangible personal property: 0.1595 in 2025.
  • Motor vehicles and boats: 0.2000 in 2025.

Under House Bill 44, a city may adopt a compensating rate, which raises about the same revenue as the year before, or go up to 4 percent more revenue after a public hearing. Anything above 4 percent can be challenged by a recall petition. A homeowner's dollar bill can still rise when the PVA raises the assessment, even with a falling rate.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Boyle County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with a conference at the PVA's office; Kentucky does not let you skip it. The assessment date is January 1, and the real property tax roll opens for public inspection on the first Monday in May for thirteen days. After a conference you have until close of business on the workday following the last inspection day to file the appeal with the county clerk.

The local board of assessment appeals meets 25 to 35 days after inspection ends and sits no more than five days without state approval. Bring evidence: sales of similar homes, an appraisal, repair estimates, insurance values or listing data. A board that receives no supporting evidence denies the appeal. An owner who skips the local board loses the right to go on to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

If bills go out before your appeal ends, the bill uses the value you claimed. A supplemental bill follows if the board lands higher.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Kentucky homestead exemption?
sections.html:
A homeowner who is 65 or older, or totally disabled under a public or private retirement system, can subtract a fixed amount from the assessed value of the home they own and live in. The Department of Revenue set that amount at $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 tax periods. The home must be owned and occupied on the January 1 assessment date.

File the application with the Boyle County PVA by December 31 of the tax year. The city of Danville names homestead exemptions for seniors as one of the services the PVA handles. If your bill shows no exemption and you qualify, speak to the PVA first.

sections.h2: What happens when a Boyle County bill is not paid?
sections.html:
After April 15 the unpaid bill moves to the county clerk as a certificate of delinquency, and a lien is recorded on the property. Interest runs at 1 percent per month. Clerk and county attorney commissions, notice postage and advertising fees stack on top. The Department of Revenue's worked example turns a $1,000 bill into $1,254 at transfer and about $1,388 within five business days after that.

The county attorney mails a 30-day notice and later a 60-day notice. The sale of unpaid certificates to third-party purchasers can be scheduled 90 to 135 days after the transfer. If you are selling a house with prior-year tax outstanding, ask the clerk for a payoff figure so the closing agent can pay it from proceeds.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work when a Boyle County house sells?
sections.html:
Kentucky bills the person who owned the property on January 1, so a house sold in March still produces a bill in the seller's name. Closing agents usually prorate the year between buyer and seller on the settlement statement, then either pay the sheriff directly or hand a credit to whoever will pay it. Mortgage servicers do not automatically receive a bill; owners with an escrow account should forward the bill to their lender.

When a house is inherited, behind on taxes, or needs work that makes a conventional listing impractical, a direct sale to a cash buyer can settle the tax in the same closing. Request the payoff from the sheriff (current year) or clerk (earlier years) before the closing date.

faqs.q: Who do I call if my Boyle County assessment looks too high?
faqs.a: Call the Boyle County PVA at 859-238-1104 before you pay. The sheriff only collects, and the clerk only receives the appeal paperwork.

faqs.q: Is the Boyle County 2% discount still available after November?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff's schedule for the 2026 bills gives the 2% discount through November 30, 2026. December brings the face amount, and January adds a 5 percent penalty.

faqs.q: Do Danville homeowners get one tax bill or two?
faqs.a: Some get two. Danville Independent district parcels receive a separate school bill, while city, county, state and Boyle County school taxes arrive on the sheriff's bill.

faqs.q: How much is the Kentucky homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The maximum is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 tax periods. It applies to homeowners 65 or older, or totally disabled, who live in the home on January 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Boyle County house that has unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask the clerk for a payoff on delinquent bills and the sheriff for the current bill amount, then have the closing agent pay both out of the sale proceeds.
